response:
Diagnosis before this batch. Three things are now established: (i) the multiplicative rank architecture with a *near-term claim* quality leg is the reliable engine (3.0–4.1% alpha, t ≈ 2.5–3.5); (ii) on the profitability side, both the level (slope 2.6–3.2) and, newly, the one-year *change* (alpha 3.3%, t 3.03) work, while margin delivers alpha without slope; (iii) long-horizon stock measures of quality keep failing — retained earnings against claims produced a 2.46 slope but −0.3% alpha, the third re-based null, so that channel is closed. A procedural lesson also arrived: an oancf-only profit leg is rejected as theme-insufficient, so cash information must be carried alongside a profitability-exclusive item. With three generations left after this one, the batch is weighted toward consolidating the profit-state/profit-news and claim-structure dimensions, plus two genuinely new channels (cash coverage inside the safety composite, and net liquid position after financial debt).

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Profit State And News Safely Funded
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Durable operating strength has a stock and a flow component — being highly profitable and getting more profitable — and both are only bankable when the firm is not dependent on short-term creditors; combining the level with the improvement identifies firms whose franchise is both strong and strengthening behind a safe funding structure.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The level leg and the change leg have now been run separately against the identical maturity leg with almost equal alpha (4.0% and 3.3%) but very different persistence and slope profiles, so this is a test of whether two economically distinct properties of the profit path — where it is and where it is going — are additive rather than an averaging of two proxies for the same latent quantity. Because the change leg is nearly uncorrelated over time with the level, the blended profitability leg should raise the information content of the long leg without the turnover cost of a pure change signal. Inputs are dense and only one lag is needed.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Improving Profits With Deep Buffers
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, at), 1)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: A rise in profitability is most likely to stick when the firm holds a deep working-capital buffer, because such a firm can reinvest and hold prices through the ensuing competitive response, whereas a liquidity-constrained firm must monetise the improvement immediately and typically gives it back.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: The profit-change leg has been tested only against debt maturity, and the working-capital buffer leg — the archive's single best on alpha (4.1%) and slope (3.20) — has been tested only against profitability levels, so this pairing is genuinely unexplored and separates whether the change leg needs maturity safety specifically or general balance-sheet slack. It also addresses the persistence critique of level-based signals: if news conditioned on buffers performs at parent level, the family is not merely a static quality tilt. Coverage matches the archive norm with one lag.
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional

---SIGNAL 3---
NAME: Cash Covered Claims And Profits
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(SUMRANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt)), RATIO(oancf, lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Obligations are settled in cash, not in accruals, so the safety of a profitable firm depends jointly on how little it owes soon and on how much operating cash it produces per dollar of total claims; the two protections should reinforce one another.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Cash-flow coverage of liabilities appeared once, in the gen-0 signal that delivered 2.2% alpha with only 0.08 coverage, and has never been combined with the maturity leg that now anchors the archive; carrying it as one of two equally weighted quality channels rather than as the sole leg limits the damage if the cash item is sparse. This is the batch's cleanest test of whether cash-based safety adds anything beyond balance-sheet composition, with coverage itself as the interpretive diagnostic. The oibdp profitability leg keeps the expression theme-valid, which the rejected cash-only construction did not.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 4---
NAME: Rising Debt Service Coverage
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(DELTA(RATIO(oibdp, lt), 1)))
HYPOTHESIS: What matters for durability is the direction of the firm's solvency position: a profitable firm whose operating profit is growing relative to its total claims — whether by earning more or by retiring obligations — is converting operating success into financial resilience, while flat or deteriorating coverage signals that profits are being absorbed by the balance sheet.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: Every flow construction that failed in this archive applied the change operator to a financing quantity alone (debt growth, payables growth), which is contaminated by investment and size; here the change is applied to the *joint* profit-to-claims ratio, so improvement can come from either side and the measure is scale-free. It is distinct from the profit-change leg because a firm can raise profitability while levering up, which this signal penalises and the pure profit change does not. Inputs are dense and only one lag is required.
INTERACTION_TYPE: novel

---SIGNAL 5---
NAME: Innovation Backed Profits Safely Funded
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(SUMRANK(RATIO(oibdp, at), RATIO(COALESCE(xrd, 0), sale))), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Profitability is most persistent when it is defended by continuing investment in the product, and such investment is only sustainable if the firm is not exposed to refinancing pressure that forces discretionary spending cuts; profitable, research-intensive, term-funded firms should therefore have the most durable earning power.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: R&D intensity is the one substantial theme resource the archive has never touched, and it supplies the economic mechanism — a defended competitive position — that the balance-sheet legs cannot express, so it is the batch's genuinely new channel rather than another recombination. Treating unreported R&D as zero is the standard and economically correct convention for firms that genuinely do no research, preserving full coverage instead of restricting the sample to reporters. If the moat channel adds nothing, the final generations can concentrate entirely on funding structure with a clear conscience.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---SIGNAL 6---
NAME: Net Liquid Position After Debt
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oibdp, at)), RANK(RATIO(SUB(SUB(act, lct), dltt), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: The correct measure of financial protection is what remains of a firm's liquid resources once every financial claim, short and long, is deducted: a profitable firm whose current assets exceed both its current liabilities and its funded debt owes its future to no one, while the same profitability with a negative net position is a residual claim behind creditors.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
REASONING: This fuses into one economic quantity the two legs that have anchored opposite ends of the archive's performance — net working capital over liabilities (best alpha, 4.1%) and financial-debt share of claims (best slope, 3.31) — rather than averaging their ranks, so it tests whether a single net-financial-position measure dominates both parents on the joint criterion. Because liquid resources and funded debt enter with opposite signs in the same numerator, the measure is monotone in exactly the direction the economic story predicts and is scale-free after division by total liabilities. All inputs are dense and no window is required.
INTERACTION_TYPE: composite

---CRITIQUE Profit State And News Safely Funded---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: This is an average of two already-tested signals against the identical maturity leg — level×NEG(dlc/lt) (alpha 4.0%, t=3.55) and delta×NEG(dlc/lt) (alpha 3.3%, t=3.03) — so the expected result is mechanically bracketed by its two parents, and the outer RANK around SUMRANK is a redundant monotone wrapper; it is a cosmetic recombination rather than a new economic hypothesis.

---CRITIQUE Improving Profits With Deep Buffers---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: An untested pairing of two archive legs whose diagnostic purpose (does the profit-change leg need maturity safety specifically or generic slack?) is legitimate and the expression matches the hypothesis, but it remains leg-swapping within a saturated family and both parents' alphas set a low ceiling on incremental information.

---CRITIQUE Cash Covered Claims And Profits---
VERDICT: flag
SCORE: 2
RATIONALE: The stated coverage defence is incorrect — SUMRANK needs both inputs, so the sparse oancf leg (0.08 in the gen-0 test) will bind the whole signal's coverage rather than being cushioned by the dense maturity leg, and the likely outcome is the archive's best-performing leg diluted and its sample halved, which is uninterpretable as evidence about cash-based safety.

---CRITIQUE Rising Debt Service Coverage---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: The construction is internally consistent and the argument that a ratio-change captures both numerator and denominator improvement is fair, but the two legs share oibdp so a large part of the product is a squared profitability term, and the deleveraging channel it adds resembles "Profits Not Propped By New Debt," which produced negative alpha.

---CRITIQUE Innovation Backed Profits Safely Funded---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 3
RATIONALE: R&D intensity is a genuinely new channel for this archive and the funding-safety interaction is economically coherent, but xrd/sale is a long-published anomaly proxy, COALESCE-to-zero creates a large tied mass at the bottom of the rank, and R&D intensity is negatively correlated with contemporaneous oibdp/at so the SUMRANK may partly cancel the profitability leg it is meant to reinforce.

---CRITIQUE Net Liquid Position After Debt---
VERDICT: accept
SCORE: 4
RATIONALE: Unlike the rest of the batch this fuses the liquidity and debt legs into a single scale-free net-financial-position quantity rather than averaging ranks, giving it a distinct functional form and a monotone economic interpretation, though it is close to the standard net-debt construct and its incremental value over the existing NWC/lt leg (alpha 4.1%) is uncertain.

---SIGNAL 1---
NAME: Return On Financed Capital With Buffers
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(oiadp, ADD(ADD(dltt, dlc), ceq))), RANK(RATIO(SUB(act, lct), lt)))
HYPOTHESIS: The economically meaningful profitability rate is the return on capital that actually has to be serviced — funded debt plus shareholders' equity — rather than the return on a total asset base that is partly financed by free operating liabilities; a high return on financed capital held by a firm with deep working-capital buffers is the clearest evidence of a franchise that earns more than its cost of capital and can survive the cycle.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: Every profitability leg in the archive has been scaled by assets or sales, so the invested-capital denominator is a genuinely new normalisation and not an average of tested signals: it mechanically rewards firms that generate profit while employing little financed capital, which is a different ordering from asset-scaled profitability whenever payables and accruals are large. Pairing it with the archive's best-performing quality leg keeps the comparison interpretable, and the two legs share no inputs, so the interaction is not double-counting. All inputs are dense annual items, so coverage should sit at the archive norm.

---SIGNAL 2---
NAME: Working Capital Adjusted Cash Profit
EXPRESSION: MUL(RANK(RATIO(SUB(oibdp, DELTA(SUB(act, lct), 1)), at)), RANK(NEG(RATIO(dlc, lt))))
HYPOTHESIS: Reported operating profit overstates durable earning power exactly when it is absorbed by a growing investment in receivables and inventory; subtracting the year's increase in net working capital yields the cash the operations actually threw off, and that cash-verified profitability is what determines whether a firm can meet claims without returning to creditors.
EXPECTED_SIGN: positive
INTERACTION_TYPE: conditional
REASONING: This delivers the cash-verification mechanism the flagged proposal was after while avoiding the coverage collapse the critic correctly identified, because the working-capital change is built from dense balance-sheet items rather than the sparse cash-flow statement item. It is also a sharper test than a cash-coverage safety leg: the adjustment enters the profitability leg itself, so the signal directly contrasts accrual profitability with cash profitability inside the architecture that works. The construction requires one lag and leaves the proven maturity leg untouched, so any change in performance is attributable solely to cash verification of profits.
